fp64_baseline: not re-run; the fp64 rows come from p1_neural_mode_sweep.csv (arm b) and p1_neural_qr.csv (arm b'), which use the same 50 seeds, 4000 iterations, I0, fixed Gauss and n_q = 256
quadrature: Gauss nodes and weights are built in fp64 and cast down, so the quadrature rule itself is not part of the precision variable
prediction: kappa_2(G) reaches 1.56e11 at k = 9 in fp64, so kappa_2(G) times the fp32 unit roundoff is of order 1e4 and the Gram path should have no significant digits left, while the QR path depends on kappa_2(Phi) = sqrt(kappa_2(G)) instead. The prediction recorded before the reduced-precision runs is in docs/paper2-cs/2026-08-26-precision-third-point-prediction.md
rescoring: per-seed records and the projected mode shapes are saved, so a change of scoring rule or reference can be applied without re-running the solves
measurement: spectral diagnostics are computed on a float64 copy of the stored span at precisions where the library provides no symmetric eigensolver; the orthonormalization itself runs at the working precision and each row records the measure_dtype actually used
added: 2026-08-26, after the pre-specified grid; the judgment rules (MAC >= 0.9, |dlambda|/lambda <= 0.05, four outcomes, 50 seeds, Wilson 95 %, 4000 iterations) were not changed
